result.topic_en: Hilbert relates simple connectedness to the single-valuedness of continuous functions, then sketches carrying Riemann's theory of multi-sheeted surfaces of algebraic functions over to n dimensions using a branching locus of dimension n-2 and cuts of dimension n-1.

items.english: [In order that single-valuedness and continuity] can be possible at the same time, it is necessary and sufficient that the space be simply connected.

items.english: If one now wants to carry Riemann's theory of the multi-sheeted 2-dimensional surfaces belonging to an algebraic function of one variable over to n dimensions, then one should consider such a space of n dimensions.
This branching locus is necessarily of n-2 dimensions.

items.english: Now one should lay down cut loci which, since they are supposed to separate the space, must necessarily be of n-1 dimensions, and which are bounded solely by the branching locus.
